info.name: Sprint 1 - Authentication
info.description:
## Sprint 1 — Authentication

This folder covers the complete **user authentication lifecycle** for the Badelha platform. All endpoints are prefixed with `/api/auth/` and handle identity management from account creation through session termination.

---

### Endpoints Overview

| Request | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Register | `POST` | `/api/auth/register` | Create a new user account. Hashes the password, sets status to `PENDING_VERIFICATION`, and returns a JWT access + refresh token pair. |
| Login | `POST` | `/api/auth/login` | Authenticate with email and password. Returns a JWT access token and sets an `HttpOnly` refresh token cookie. |
| Logout | `POST` | `/api/auth/logout` | Invalidate the current session and clear the refresh token cookie. |
| Refresh Token | `POST` | `/api/auth/refresh-token` | Issue a new JWT access token using the `HttpOnly` refresh token cookie. Rotates the refresh token on every call. |
| Verify Email | `POST` | `/api/auth/verify-email` | Confirm a user's email address using the verification token sent after registration. |
| Forgot Password | `POST` | `/api/auth/forgot-password` | Initiate the password reset flow by sending a reset link to the user's email. |
| Reset Password | `POST` | `/api/auth/reset-password` | Complete the password reset using the token received by email. |
| Get Profile | `GET` | `/api/auth/profile` | Retrieve the authenticated user's profile information. Requires a valid JWT access token. |

---

### Token Strategy

- **Access Token** — Short-lived JWT returned in the response body. Must be attached to protected requests via the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
- **Refresh Token** — Long-lived token (30-day TTL) stored in an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie scoped to `/api/auth/refresh-token`. Automatically rotated on each refresh call.

---

### Notes

- After-response scripts automatically save `accessToken` and `refreshToken` to the active environment for seamless chaining with downstream requests.
- Account status (`ACTIVE`, `PENDING_VERIFICATION`, `BANNED`, `SUSPENDED`) is enforced on login and token refresh.
- Password hashes are never exposed in any response.

item.name: register user
item.description:
### Register User

**Endpoint**

POST /api/auth/register

**Description**

Registers a new user account in the Badelha platform. On success, a new user record is created with `account_status` set to `PENDING_VERIFICATION` and `is_verified` set to `false`. A JWT access token and refresh token are returned immediately so the user can interact with the API before verifying their email.

A verification email is sent automatically to the provided address after registration. Use the `/api/auth/verify-email` endpoint with the token from that email to activate the account.

> 📧 In development mode, the verification token can be retrieved programmatically via `GET /api/auth/dev/email-verification-token?email=<email>` — this is used automatically by the Postman pre-request script.

---

### Request Body

```json
{
  "fullName": "John Doe",
  "phoneNumber": "0599123456",
  "address": "Ramallah, Palestine",
  "email": "john@example.com",
  "password": "Secret@123",
  "cityId": 1
}
```

---

### Validation Rules

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `fullName` | Required · 3–100 characters |
| `phoneNumber` | Required · Valid Palestinian format (`05XXXXXXXX`) · Exactly 10 digits |
| `address` | Required · 5–255 characters |
| `email` | Required · Valid email format |
| `password` | Required · Min 8 chars · Uppercase · Lowercase · Number · Special character (`!@#$%^&*` etc.) |
| `cityId` | Required · Positive integer |

---

### Success Response — `201 Created`

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 201,
  "message": "User registered successfully",
  "data": {
    "user": {
      "user_id": 1,
      "full_name": "John Doe",
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "phone_number": "0599123456",
      "address": "Ramallah, Palestine",
      "city_id": 1,
      "account_status": "PENDING_VERIFICATION",
      "is_verified": false,
      "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      "city": { "city_id": 1, "city_name": "Nablus" }
    },
    "accessToken": "<jwt_access_token>",
    "refreshToken": "<jwt_refresh_token>"
  }
}
```

> 🍪 The `refreshToken` is also set as an `HttpOnly` cookie scoped to `/api/auth/refresh-token` (30-day expiry).

---

### Error Responses

| Status | Message | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `400 Bad Request` | Validation error | Missing or invalid fields |
| `409 Conflict` | Email already exists | An account with this email is already registered |
| `409 Conflict` | Phone number already exists | An account with this phone number is already registered |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | Internal server error | Unexpected server-side failure |

item.name: login
item.description:
### Login User

**Endpoint**

POST /api/auth/login

**Description**

Authenticates an existing user with their email and password. Returns a JWT access token and sets an `HttpOnly` cookie containing the refresh token. Also updates the user's `last_login` timestamp.

> ⚠️ The account must not be banned or suspended. Email verification is not required to log in, but account status is checked.

---

### Request Body

```json
{
  "email": "john@example.com",
  "password": "Secret@123"
}
```

---

### Validation Rules

| Field | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| `email` | Required · Valid email format |
| `password` | Required · Minimum 8 characters |

---

### Success Response — `200 OK`

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "Login successful",
  "data": {
    "user": {
      "user_id": 1,
      "full_name": "John Doe",
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "phone_number": "0599123456",
      "address": "Ramallah, Palestine",
      "city_id": 3,
      "account_status": "ACTIVE",
      "is_verified": true,
      "last_login": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      "total_transactions": 5,
      "city": { "city_id": 3, "city_name": "Ramallah" },
      "user_roles": [{ "role_id": 1, "role": { "role_name": "USER" } }]
    },
    "accessToken": "<jwt_access_token>",
    "refreshToken": "<jwt_refresh_token>"
  }
}
```

> 🍪 A `refreshToken` cookie is also set automatically (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, 30-day expiry, scoped to `/api/auth/refresh-token`).

---

### Error Responses

| Status | Message | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400 Bad Request` | Validation error | Missing or invalid fields |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Invalid email or password | Credentials do not match |
| `403 Forbidden` | Account is banned | User account has been banned |
| `403 Forbidden` | Account is suspended | User account has been suspended |

item.name: refresh token
item.description:
### Refresh Access Token

**Endpoint**

POST /api/auth/refresh-token

**Description**

Issues a new pair of JWT access token and refresh token using the existing refresh token stored in the `refreshToken` HttpOnly cookie. The old refresh token is invalidated and replaced with a new one in the database.

> 🍪 This endpoint reads the refresh token from the `refreshToken` cookie automatically set during login or registration. No request body is needed.

> ⚠️ The refresh token must be valid, not expired (30-day TTL), and must match the one stored in the database for the user. Banned accounts are rejected.

---

### Request Body

No request body required. The refresh token is read from the `refreshToken` cookie.

---

### Authentication

| Type | Details |
|---|---|
| Cookie | `refreshToken` — HttpOnly cookie set by `/api/auth/login` or `/api/auth/register` |

---

### Success Response — `200 OK`

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "Token refreshed successfully",
  "data": {
    "accessToken": "<new_jwt_access_token>",
    "refreshToken": "<new_jwt_refresh_token>"
  }
}
```

---

### Error Responses

| Status | Message | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `401 Unauthorized` | Refresh token required | Cookie is missing |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Invalid or expired token | Token is invalid, expired, or does not match the stored token |
| `403 Forbidden` | Account is banned | User account has been banned |

exec: pm.test("Response has success flag set to true", function () {
console.log("✅ accessToken updated in environment from refresh-token.");

item.name: verify email
item.description:
### Verify Email

**Endpoint**

GET /api/auth/verify-email?token=<verification_token>

**Description**

Verifies a user's email address using the token sent to their inbox after registration. On success, the user's `is_verified` flag is set to `true` and their `account_status` is updated from `PENDING_VERIFICATION` to `ACTIVE`.

The verification token is single-use and expires after **24 hours**. Once used, the token is marked as `is_used = true` and cannot be reused.

> 📧 The verification email is sent automatically after a successful `/api/auth/register` call.

---

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `token` | string | ✅ | The verification token received in the email |

---

### Validation Rules

- `token` query parameter must be present in the request URL.
- Token must exist in the database, not be used (`is_used = false`), and not be expired (`expires_at > now`).

---

### Success Response — `200 OK`

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "Email verified successfully",
  "data": {
    "message": "Email verified successfully"
  }
}
```

---

### Error Responses

| Status | Message | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `400 Bad Request` | Verification token required | `token` query param is missing |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid or expired token | Token not found, already used, or expired |

item.name: forgot password
item.description:
### Forgot Password

**Endpoint**

POST /api/auth/forgot-password

**Description**

Initiates the password reset flow for a registered user. Sends a password reset email containing a one-time token to the provided email address.

Any previously unused reset tokens for the user are invalidated before a new one is created. The new token expires after **1 hour**.

> ℹ️ For security reasons, if the email is not found in the system, a `404` error is returned. In production, consider returning a generic success message regardless to avoid user enumeration.

---

### Request Body

```json
{
  "email": "john@example.com"
}
```

---

### Validation Rules

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `email` | Required · Valid email format |

---

### Success Response — `200 OK`

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "Password reset email sent",
  "data": {
    "message": "Password reset email sent"
  }
}
```

> 📧 A password reset email is sent to the provided address with a link containing the reset token. Use that token in the `/api/auth/reset-password` endpoint.

---

### Error Responses

| Status | Message | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `400 Bad Request` | Validation error | Missing or invalid email |
| `404 Not Found` | User not found | No account exists with the given email |

item.name: reset password
item.description:
### Reset Password

**Endpoint**

POST /api/auth/reset-password

**Description**

Resets the user's password using the one-time token received via email from the `/api/auth/forgot-password` endpoint. On success, the token is marked as used and the user's password is updated with the new hashed password.

> ⚠️ The reset token expires after **1 hour** and can only be used **once**. Request a new token via `/api/auth/forgot-password` if it has expired.

---

### Request Body

```json
{
  "token": "a3f8c2e1d4b7f9e0c6a1b2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3",
  "password": "NewSecret@456"
}
```

---

### Validation Rules

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `token` | Required · Minimum 32 characters |
| `password` | Required · Min 8 chars · Must include uppercase letter · Must include lowercase letter · Must include a number |

---

### Success Response — `200 OK`

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "Password reset successfully",
  "data": {
    "message": "Password reset successfully"
  }
}
```

---

### Error Responses

| Status | Message | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `400 Bad Request` | Validation error | Missing fields or password does not meet requirements |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid or expired token | Token not found, already used, or expired (> 1 hour) |

exec: pm.test("Response has success flag set to true", function () {
pm.test("Response data contains message field", function () {

item.name: get profile
item.description:
### Get User Profile

**Endpoint**

GET /api/auth/profile

**Description**

Returns the full profile of the currently authenticated user, including personal details, city, assigned roles, and their average rating on the platform.

> 🔒 This is a **protected route**. A valid JWT access token must be provided in the `Authorization` header as a Bearer token.

---

### Authentication

| Type | Header | Format |
|---|---|---|
| Bearer Token | `Authorization` | `Bearer <jwt_access_token>` |

Obtain the access token from `/api/auth/login` or `/api/auth/register`.

> ⚠️ The token is verified against the JWT secret. Expired or invalid tokens return `401`. Banned or suspended accounts return `403`.

---

### Request Body

No request body required.

---

### Success Response — `200 OK`

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "Profile retrieved successfully",
  "data": {
    "user_id": 1,
    "full_name": "John Doe",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "phone_number": "0599123456",
    "address": "Ramallah, Palestine",
    "city_id": 3,
    "account_status": "ACTIVE",
    "is_verified": true,
    "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "last_login": "2024-06-01T10:00:00.000Z",
    "total_transactions": 12,
    "city": { "city_id": 3, "city_name": "Ramallah" },
    "user_roles": [{ "role_id": 1, "role": { "role_name": "USER" } }],
    "average_rating": 4.5
  }
}
```

---

### Error Responses

| Status | Message | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `401 Unauthorized` | Authentication required | `Authorization` header is missing |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Invalid token | Token is malformed or invalid |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Token expired | JWT access token has expired — use `/api/auth/refresh-token` |
| `403 Forbidden` | Account is banned | User account has been banned |
| `403 Forbidden` | Account is suspended | User account has been suspended |
| `404 Not Found` | User not found | Authenticated user no longer exists in the database |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | Internal server error | Unexpected server-side failure |

item.name: logout
item.description:
### Logout User

**Endpoint**

POST /api/auth/logout

**Description**

Logs out the currently authenticated user by clearing their refresh token from the database and removing the `refreshToken` HttpOnly cookie. After logout, the refresh token is no longer valid and cannot be used to obtain new access tokens.

> 🔒 This is a **protected route**. A valid JWT access token must be provided in the `Authorization` header as a Bearer token.

> ℹ️ The access token itself is not invalidated server-side (it remains valid until it naturally expires). To fully secure a session, clients should discard the access token on their end after logout.

---

### Authentication

| Type | Header | Format |
|---|---|---|
| Bearer Token | `Authorization` | `Bearer <jwt_access_token>` |

---

### Request Body

No request body required.

---

### Success Response — `200 OK`

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "Logout successful",
  "data": null
}
```

> 🍪 The `refreshToken` cookie is cleared automatically on the client (scoped to `/api/auth/refresh-token`).

---

### Error Responses

| Status | Message | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `401 Unauthorized` | Authentication required | `Authorization` header is missing |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Invalid token | Token is malformed or invalid |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Token expired | JWT access token has expired — use `/api/auth/refresh-token` first |
| `403 Forbidden` | Account is banned | User account has been banned |
| `403 Forbidden` | Account is suspended | User account has been suspended |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | Internal server error | Unexpected server-side failure |

pm.test("Response message is Logout successful", function () {
console.log("✅ accessToken cleared from environment after logout.");
